name: ChromaGrid-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Two cards are fully lit in their real colours while the rest stay grey, showing the reveal at its peak.

tagline: A wall of grey portraits turns to colour under the cursor.
summary: Six people cards sit in a neat grid, all greyscale at rest. Moving the pointer across them lifts the grey in a soft circular window, exposing each photo and its coloured card gradient.
appearance: Two rows of three rounded cards, each holding a square portrait above a name, an @handle on the right and a job title below. At rest every photo is grey and the gaps between cards read as near-black.
behaviour: A circle of colour travels with the pointer, clearing the grey overlay only around the cursor. When the pointer leaves, the whole grid fades back to monochrome.
demo_content: Six stock portraits named Alex Rivera, Jordan Chen, Morgan Blake and others, each with a job title and an @handle.
search_phrases: greyscale team cards that colour on hover
photo grid reveals colour near cursor
black and white portraits turn colorful
team page grid with hover reveal
grey photos light up under the mouse
use_when: A team or people grid should feel alive without video, extra images or a click.
avoid_when: It needs a pointer, so touch users only ever see the flat grey version of every card.
customise: Cards come from an items array of image, title, subtitle, handle, location, border colour, gradient and link; radius, damping, fade and easing are props.
weight_why: A full-cover backdrop-filter mask is repainted on every pointer move across six cards.

a11y.note: Each card is a clickable article with no tab stop, role or key handler, so the external links cannot be reached without a mouse.

issues: Clicking anywhere on a card opens an external site, with no visible link affordance.
polish_why: Sharp portraits and a smooth spotlight reveal, though the resting grey grid is quite dim.
title: ChromaGrid
